detail: First message A->B delivered (authenticated receipt) 371 ms after send; first B->A 523 ms (1 message, measured on the box). Both on an already-warm mesh (nodes had been up several minutes), so not a cold-start figure.

A -> B via MCP send_message over stdio (agentnet-acceptance mcp-call, negotiated protocol 2026-07-28): queued, then status delivered (delivered_at - created_at = 397 ms). evidence/mcp-send.json, mcp-status.json. MCP only exercised on A (Mac); not on B.

A->B delivered 20/20 (authenticated receipts), send->receipt (receipt observed by polling status every 100 ms) p50/p95/p99 = 427/855/855 ms (min 413, max 855), paced 400 ms, run concurrently with B->A. n=20 so p95 and p99 equal the max.

B->A delivered 20/20, p50/p95/p99 = 811/901/901 ms (min 406, max 901), same conditions. Receiver inbox rows 20, unique 20 in both directions (no duplicates). Latency includes sequential status polling in the harness (about +100-400 ms).

Agent B daemon and node B stopped on the box; A sent 10 messages (5 intended plus 5 extra from a shell error in the harness; all 10 stayed 'sent', none delivered while B was off). Node B started, then agent B: all 10 delivered with receipts 3.7 s after the node start command (includes ~3 s of ssh exec overhead and a 2 s sleep); B inbox 10 rows, 10 unique. Messages came via R's Store sync. Node B was a stop/start of the same container (not recreated), so the 62 s recreated-node blind window did not apply.
command: docker stop an-nb; pkill agentnet serve (box); agentnet send x10 (Mac); docker start an-nb; agentnet serve (box)

detail: Mac: node A's libp2p port (tcp/60000 in the container) is NOT published (docker ports: 8545/tcp, 30303/tcp, 60000/tcp unpublished; only 127.0.0.1:18650->8645 REST). lsof LISTEN shows only loopback listeners (the SSH tunnel on 127.0.0.1:61660, colima's REST forward on 127.0.0.1:18650); nothing on 60000; nc to 127.0.0.1:60000 fails. A made only outbound connections: through the tunnel from behind the home NAT.

Box: 'instabox port ls' shows ports: [] (nothing published; instabox port publish never used). ss -ltnp shows listeners only on 127.0.0.1 (R libp2p 60000, R REST 18640, B REST 18642) and sshd on :22. eth0 is a private 172.16.0.2/30 address (no public address on the box interface). R's libp2p port is reachable from the Mac only via the instabox port-forward SSH tunnel.
command: instabox port ls agentnet-xhost ; ss -ltnp ; ip -4 -o addr (on the box)

detail: GET /admin/v1/peers on R lists A as /ip4/172.28.66.1/tcp/<ephemeral>: the box's docker bridge gateway, i.e. the tunnel's far end (sshd -> docker-proxy), NOT the Mac's NAT address. R therefore has no knowledge of the Mac's address.

A direct TCP connect from the Mac to the box's public address on the libp2p port was NOT run: the sandbox service does not reveal a public address for the box (instabox get shows none; the box NIC is private), so there was no address to probe. The evidence is 'no port published' plus the box's loopback-only listeners.

SINGLE TRIAL. Port-forward killed (tunnel down ~123 s). R saw A drop within 10 s (peer state CanConnect, then CannotConnect): the SSH forward closes the TCP connection cleanly, so R did NOT hold a stale socket (established sockets on 60000 fell 2 -> 1 within 10 s); the tcp_retries2=6 setting was therefore not exercised by this failure mode. A queued message (NoPeersToPublish while down, state queued, attempts 0). After the tunnel was restored: A listed R Connected after 4.2 s; the queued message was delivered (receipt) after 49.5 s (the rest is relay-mesh re-establishment and the sender retry timer). A silent blackhole (packet drop, as in the wireguard simulation) was not tested here.
command: kill <instabox port-forward>; sleep 120; instabox port-forward agentnet-xhost 61660:60000

detail: Silent path failure (packets dropped without FIN/RST) across the real hosts was not run; only a clean tunnel close was.
libp2p NAT traversal / hole punching, direct public-internet libp2p, relay-to-client dial-back: not applicable to this topology (client-to-relay is carried inside an SSH tunnel) and not tested.
